comment: Declared surfaces whose merge, in a repo where merging triggers automation on the
default branch, PERFORMS a real-world action rather than publishing code: it
provisions/mutates/destroys billable infrastructure, moves money, or is one-way.
Read by ai/bin/blast-radius, which is called by integration-gate before a merge.
Patterns are deliberately GENERIC (no product repo is named here). This file
lives in ~/dev/custom and classifies other repos by reading them, never by
requiring anything to be committed into them.
Adding a pattern only ever WIDENS what is held for the owner, which is always
safe. NEVER narrow or remove a pattern to make a merge pass
(ai/blocks/ops/safety-checks.md) -- excluding a path to go green is the named
forbidden move, and here it would silently restore the exact hole this exists to
close. If a pattern is genuinely wrong, the OWNER decides, and the change cites
the evidence.

surfaces.why: merging applies it: provisions, mutates or destroys real, billable cloud resources
merging changes what EVERY future merge does -- the machinery that performs the action

merging RUNS it: the migration executes on the deploy that merging triggers, and irreversibly destroys data. Ecto reversibility restores the SCHEMA, never the rows -- `remove :col, :type` in a `change` block is auto-reversible in Ecto's sense and every value in that column is still gone the moment it runs. NEVER use Ecto-reversibility to downgrade a hit here.

comment: This surface is CONTENT-gated: a path hit alone is NOT a surface hit.
Routine migrations (create table, add column, create index) touch these
paths on every feature MR and must stay COLD.
Measured 2026-09-20 over 364 migrations in gen_saas + walt_ui: a naive
verb rule (drop|remove anywhere) flags 59 and is ~50% precise on walt_ui,
gating `drop constraint` x15 and `drop index` x4, which lose no data.
This rule flags far fewer, and only where rows are actually destroyed.
Content is read from the file AT HEAD (git show <head>:<path>), never
from diff text: a diff hunk may not show the `def down` line, which
would make the up/down distinction undecidable. A file absent at head
was DELETED and does not execute on deploy -- not a hit, but PRINTED,
never silently skipped. Any other read failure is a hit (fail closed).

exclude_first.why: dropping an index or a constraint loses no rows; it is mechanically rebuildable by its inverse. This exclusion is what keeps routine schema hygiene ungated.

match_line.why: drops a table and every row in it
drops a column and every value in it
a `drop` whose argument this rule does not recognise -- the argument is what decides whether rows are lost, so an unrecognised argument is UNDECIDABLE and fails closed

match_region.why: raw destructive SQL in an `execute`. Scanned region-wide, not per-line, so heredocs are covered.

known_gaps: A lossy `modify` (narrowing a column type so Postgres truncates on cast) is NOT detected. Most `modify` calls are benign (null, default) and no pattern separates them, so this is a NAMED gap rather than a silent one; the captain's `Blast radius: IRREVERSIBLE` channel is its only cover.
A `drop table` on a table created earlier in the SAME migration is a hit, though it destroys nothing. Rare; fails closed by design.
